This wasn't supported from the beginning as properties where always implicitly defined by just assigning them, e.g like so ```js class Foo { definedPropertyA; definedPropertyB = 2; constructor() { this.implictPropertyA = 3; } } ``` The default of emitting modern JS from TS is to define properties. However, there are problems when a defined property depends on a constructor property. Those only exist in TS and are incompatible with JS and therefore TS has the `useDefineForClassFields` compiler option which we have set to `false`. However, this option will eventually be removed and only classes with defined properties are going to be supported. Problematic code is something like this ```ts // TS input class Foo { oops = this.blah + 1; // depends on this.blah constructor(public blah: number) {} } // JS output TODAY (declared props) class Foo { constructor(blah) { this.blah = blah; this.oops = this.blah + 1; } } // JS output FUTURE (defined props) class Foo { blah; oops = this.blah + 1; // ERRORS here constructor(blah) { this.blah = blah; } } ``` This issue to fix problematic usages. Thanks to @rbuckton we have a handy tool to identify them and we have list of violations that needs fixing. However, there is one issue that makes VSCode often difficult to use with VoiceOver. Normally, I use the VoiceOver modifier keys Control + Option and the arrow keys; QuickNav; and Trackpad Commander to navigate and edit text. These are three different ways of navigating, and they are normally all aligned with each other as well as with the keyboard-focus (system-focus). As for the keyboard-focus:When I Press only single arrow keys without modifier, or only the option key and one of the arrow keys, I would move the keyboard-focus. So in most cases, pressing Option + Right Arrow does the same as pressing Ctrl + Option + Right Arrow, or swiping right on the trackpad. In most text-editors, also the keyboard-focus is aligned with the VoiceOver focus. If I press Option + Right Arrow, I will jump to the next word, and then I can press Ctrl + Option + Right Arrow to keep navigating furhter; that is, I can use these keys interachangeably. For example, if trackpad-commander enabled, and I swipe to the right on the trackpad, it will remove me one word to the right, and also the keyboard focus will follow. I can then press, for instance, the Right Arrow key as a single key, and in this way I navigate character by character within the word that I just moved to. In most text editors, this works well. For example, in Apple's TextEdit or the code editor TextMate, but also in XCode, the keyboard focus and VoiceOver focus follow each other. In contrast, in VSCode they often get misaligned. For example, after using the symbols menu to jump to a section of the document, either keyboard focus or VoiceOver focus remains at the beginning of document. Even though my screen reader announces the section that I have moved to, I would actually type something at the beginning of the document. Likewise, after auto completion the same happens. The keyboard focus Will remain at the beginning of the line or somewhere in the middle, whereas the screenreader focus moves on. Thereafter, I have to turn VoiceOver off and on and then interact with the quote editor to make them aligned again. That would be really great improvement of somebody could fix this issue because VSCode is otherwise a very versatile and efficient app! This problem is not only limited to the Latex extension, but here it is particularly important. It also happens when I added Python or R code. Symbols menu: I normally navigate sections of a Latex document via the Symbols menu - Command - Shift - period (i.e., fullstop). To find the section in the symbols menu, I just Arrow down or up. Then just hit enter. This works well, but after pressing Enter I have to do a specific sequence of key presses to move the VoiceOver-focus to the keyboard-focus. To navigate the symbols menu while keeping VoiceOver focus and keyboard-focus aligned, I do the following: After using Command + Shift + ., Hit enter. Press right arrow (or any single arrow key without modifier). Then interact. Then use VO-modifier and arrow keys. Now the VoiceOver focus (i.e., the focus when I use the VoiceOver modifier keys Control + Option and the arrow keys; QuickNav; and Trackpad Commander) should be aligned with the keyboard-focus. Then I can keep editing and I do not have to worry about loosing the focus for some time.. It is worth noting that such a misalignment between screenreader-focus and system-focus is a VSCode-specific issue and does not happen in the other text editors that I am using, such as Apple's Textedit, the Open source text editor TextMate, and XCode. Here, the VoiceOver focus and keyboard-focus (system-focus) usually follow each other smoothly. If I used a trackpad to move to the next sentence, the keyboard focus Will also be on the next sentence. TextMate and XCode also have the advantage that I can use the rotor in a Latex document and jump between symbols. This is similar to the symbols menu in VSCode (Cmd + Shift + .), but here I press Ctrl + Option + U or rotate clockwise or anticlockwise with two fingers on the trackpad to bring up the rotor. Now I can select different ways of navigation, such as read next character, word, line, sentence, paragraph; and find next heading, next symbol etc. In the case of TextMate, the symbols menu shows all the document sections if I am editing a latex document. For example, it shows the backslash section 1, 2 etc. Once I have selected "symbols" in the rotor, I just need to swipe down on the trackpad with one finger and it will bring me to the next section of my document, which is very convenient. Likewise, I can bring up the rotor, something, and it will filter the displayed symbols based on the string that I typed. An autosuggestion (e.g., for `pwd`) should appear. 4. **Finalize Suggestion:** Type `d`. 5. **Observe Bug:** The prompt (`Line1\n> `) is rapidly redrawn on new lines below the `pwd` input line. The typed command remains editable, but the terminal is spammed with prompt redraws. **Expected Behavior:** The prompt should remain static. Typing `d` should finalize the command to `pwd` and potentially show a new autosuggestion, without any prompt redrawing spam. **Actual Behavior:** The prompt (`Line1\n> `) rapidly redraws on new lines below the current input line, creating a "spamming" effect. **Recording:** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af76ea8a-30f2-483d-a6e8-0b5e8fbd74e1 **Detailed Explanation & Diagnosis:** * The bug **only** occurs when all three conditions (VI Mode, Autosuggestions Enabled, Multi-line Prompt via explicit `\n`) are met simultaneously. Disabling any one of these conditions prevents the bug. * Disabling VI Mode (`set -eU fish_key_bindings`) works. * Disabling Autosuggestions (`set -U fish_autosuggestion_enabled 0`) works. * Using a single-line prompt (e.g., `echo -n -s 'Prompt> '`) works. * The issue does **not** occur in other terminal emulators (tested: macOS Terminal, WezTerm). * The issue does **not** occur with Fish's default built-in prompt. * The trigger appears related to the **finalization of an autosuggestion via character input** in VI insert mode. Explicitly accepting the entire suggestion with `Alt+F` (or equivalent `accept-autosuggestion` binding) does not trigger the bug. * Disabling the visual VI mode indicator (`functions -e fish_mode_prompt`) does **not** fix the issue. * Changing syntax highlighting colors (`fish_color_*` variables) does **not** fix the issue. * Even overriding *all* printable character keys in VI insert mode to use the Emacs-style `self-insert` function (via `fish_user_key_bindings`) does **not** fix the issue. This suggests the bug relates to the fundamental state/operation of Fish in VI mode within VS Code, not just the specific repaint strategy of VI's default self-insert action. **Hypothesis:** VS Code's integrated terminal's parsing/rendering logic for shell integration likely gets into an unstable state when a Fish prompt function outputs an explicit newline. Makes it very maintainable.","ts":"2025-05-13T03:04:58Z","value":null},{"entity":"microsoft/vscode","kind":"issue","meta":{"action":"opened","actor":"TylerLeonhardt","archive_created_at":"2025-05-13T03:43:20Z","archive_hour":"2025-05-13T03:00:00Z","author":"TylerLeonhardt","issue_created_at":"2025-05-13T03:43:17Z","issue_number":248775,"labels":["feature-request","api-proposal","authentication"],"source":"gharchive","source_event_id":"49644947563","source_event_type":"IssuesEvent","url":"https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/248775"},"text":"API to resolve scopes to auth provider ## Context In MCP land, and general OAuth land, we resolve what kind auth an MCP server needs by resolving to some OAuth Server Metadata. The important stuff in this is: ```ts /** * Metadata about an OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server. */ export interface IAuthorizationServerMetadata { /** * REQUIRED. The authorization server's issuer identifier URL that uses https scheme and has no query or fragment components. */ issuer: string; /** * URL of the authorization server's authorization endpoint. * This is REQUIRED unless no grant types are supported that use the authorization endpoint. */ authorization_endpoint?: string; /** * URL of the authorization server's token endpoint. * This is REQUIRED unless only the implicit grant type is supported. */ token_endpoint?: string; /** * OPTIONAL. URL of the authorization server's OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration endpoint. */ registration_endpoint?: string; /** * RECOMMENDED. JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 scope values supported. */ scopes_supported?: string[]; /** * REQUIRED. JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 response_type values supported. */ response_types_supported: string[]; } ``` From this, we plan on mapping issuers to auth providers. So for example, if we see an issuer like so: ``` https://github.com/login/oauth ``` we will use the `github` auth provider. `microsoft` is where it gets interesting... because technically it is N issuers all it one based on the path of issuer. ``` https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/v2.0 https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0 https://login.microsoftonline.com/consumers/v2.0 https://login.microsoftonline.com/SOME_TENANT_ID/v2.0 ``` These are all valid issuers. By default, VS Code uses `organizations`, but you can override it with a secret scope: `VSCODE_TENANT:` so like `VSCODE_TENANT:common` or `VSCODE_TENANT:`. The issuer is then used to make urls like: ``` https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0/authorize ``` which is the login page you see in your browser. and ``` https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0/token ``` which is what you use to get a token after your browser redirects back to VS Code with a code. ## Proposal ### Option 1: Leaning in to `VSCODE_TENANT` We have a `resolveMcpAuthenticationScopes` which is passed in the `authorizationServer` (aka `issuer`) and the `scopes` (aka `scopes_supported`) ```ts declare module 'vscode' { export interface AuthenticationProvider { resolveMcpAuthenticationScopes?(authorizationServer: Uri, scopes: string[], token: CancellationToken): ProviderResult; } } ``` This will resolve the correct scopes. So: * issuer: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/consumers/v2.0` * `["api://foo/bar"]` resolves to: ``` ["api://foo/bar", "VSCODE_TENANT:consumers"] ``` Then the Microsoft auth provider will have the correct scopes to build the request. ### Option 2: Making tenant first class This is more work but maybe the direction we want to go... ```ts export interface AuthenticationProviderOptions { /** * When specified, the caller of `getSession` will be able to override the issuer URL used to * authenticate the user. */ readonly supportsIssuerOverride?: boolean; } export interface AuthenticationProviderSessionOptions { /** * When specified, the authentication provider will use the provided issuer URL to * authenticate the user. This is only used when a provider `supportsIssuerOverride` is set to true */ issuer?: Uri; } export interface AuthenticationGetSessionOptions { /** * When specified, the authentication provider will use the provided issuer URL to * authenticate the user. This is only used when a provider `supportsIssuerOverride` is set to true */ issuer?: Uri; } ``` and then we implement this in the Microsoft auth provider where the tenant is extracted from `issuer` and used as a replacement for `VSCODE_TENANT`.","ts":"2025-05-13T03:43:20Z","value":null},{"entity":"microsoft/vscode","kind":"comment","meta":{"action":"created","actor":"hpe-ykoehler","archive_created_at":"2025-05-13T04:23:18Z","archive_hour":"2025-05-13T04:00:00Z","author":"hpe-ykoehler","author_association":"NONE","comment_created_at":"2025-05-13T04:23:17Z","comment_id":2875012137,"issue_number":248659,"source":"gharchive","source_event_id":"49645723510","source_event_type":"IssueCommentEvent","url":"https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/248659#issuecomment-2875012137"},"text":"From today's usage, GPT 4.1 is ignoring my copilot-instructions.md Claude seems to take care of it but only in a new chat and the first prompt.
